subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK, command-cron, and skill tool-dispatch paths, and what gates should each require?
rationale: The unresolved slices involve host filesystem, exec-class, cron, CLI/slash, and startup-readiness boundaries where automation cannot choose the acceptable security and product contract.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
options.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker while reviewing open read/write/readiness PRs individually with explicit owner/config gates, docs, audit, and live proof.

options.title: Declare shipped surfaces sufficient
options.body: Close this issue after rejecting or moving the remaining host-FS, exec, CLI/slash, and generic cron-tool-call requests out of core.

options.title: Approve a broader direct-execution design
options.body: Require a formal security design before allowing broad direct dispatch for high-power tools across CLI, slash, cron, and Gateway surfaces.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow gated slices
recommendation.body: Use this issue as the canonical tracker while reviewing open read/write/readiness PRs individually with explicit owner/config gates, docs, audit, and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent security-boundary and operator-doc history makes this the best available owner signal for the remaining maintainer choice.
